name: Suppress with fire
summary: On a key, the unit pours out a long stream of heavy fire over an area or at one target. Enemy soldiers caught in it are suppressed: they move slowly, aim badly and, if they stay under it, are pinned and can barely act until the fire stops or they crawl out. The fire still hurts as usual, but its real job is to hold enemies in place for teammates who flank or finish them. The shooter usually pays with a lock-in: it roots itself, fires less accurately, or is busy for the burst. Vehicles and crews behind armour mostly ignore it. It is the ability home of the suppress weapon trait: a gun that suppresses with every ordinary burst uses the trait instead.
counterplay: Get out of the beaten zone, or into hard cover or a building, before you are pinned; the effect builds while you stay under the fire.
Answer with something that needs no aim: grenades, mortars and other lobbed fire still land while you are pinned.
Send armour or a fast flanker at the shooter from outside its arc: it is rooted or busy for the burst, and vehicles shrug the suppression off.
Wait it out behind cover: the burst is timed and the key has a long wait, so the window to push opens right after it ends.

other_examples.note: Once the side owns the automatic-rifle upgrade, the squad can pay munitions for a short burst in which its guns suppress enemy infantry far more and fire faster, but hit much less often; the wait between uses is only a little longer than the burst. It quickly pins enemy squads so a second squad can move round and kill them, while soldiers inside buildings are not suppressed at all.

sources.title: Riflemen Squad, Company of Heroes Wiki (Fandom)

other_examples.note: For a few munitions, the squad concentrates its fire on one enemy squad for a short time and suppresses it gradually; it works better when the squad is equipped with automatic weapons (BARs or an M1919 light machine gun in its weapon slots). A one-target version of the pattern.

sources.title: Rear Echelon Troops, Company of Heroes Wiki (Fandom)
sources.note: The page is marked as under construction.

other_examples.note: With their heavy gun upgrade, the Ork squad can spend a little of the side's resource to suppress one enemy infantry unit, on a long wait. In this game suppression means the victim's courage has run out: it moves very slowly and can hardly fight back until courage returns; a few abilities and the fall-back order break it, and vehicles, plus some special heroes and heavy infantry such as Terminators, cannot be suppressed.

sources.title: Retribution/Aiming? Wotz Dat?, Dawn of War Wiki (Fandom)

sources.title: Dawn of War II combat, Dawn of War Wiki (Fandom)
sources.note: What suppression does to a unit, what breaks it and who is immune.

other_examples.unit: Suppression (Heavy and Support soldiers, SHIVs, some aliens)
other_examples.note: A barrage at one enemy that spends extra ammunition: the target's aim drops sharply, and if it moves, the suppressing unit takes a free reaction shot at it; the barrage can also wreck the target's cover. A later perk widens it to a small area. The pinned target often answers with attacks that need no aim roll, such as grenades or psionics, which the penalty does not touch.

sources.title: Suppression, XCOM Wiki (Fandom)
sources.version: XCOM: Enemy Unknown and its Enemy Within expansion

player_translation.summary: A heavy gunner who, on a key, turns its gun into a hose: for a few seconds it sprays a lane or a chosen enemy, and enemy soldiers caught in it slow to a crawl and lose their aim, so teammates can walk round and finish them. The gunner pays by standing still or firing wildly while it lasts.
as_user: Press the key and sweep a lane, a doorway or a crossing: enemy infantry there either dive for cover or get pinned in the open.
You are not trying to kill with it; you are buying your team a few seconds in which the enemy cannot move or shoot back well.
While it lasts you are rooted (or much less accurate), so pick the moment and the angle: a flanker you did not see can walk up to your side.
Call the push as you fire: the pinned enemy is easy prey for a teammate's grenade or a flank.
as_target: A loud stream of tracers and a growing pinned marker on your own character warn you before you are fully pinned.
Under the fire you move slowly and your aim wobbles; once pinned you can only crawl, so break line of sight or reach hard cover early.
Throw a grenade or call lobbed fire on the gunner: it needs no steady aim, and the gunner is standing still.
In a vehicle you shrug it off, so armour is the natural answer to a gunner holding a lane.
teammates: Setup and finisher: the gunner pins, teammates flank or throw explosives into the pinned group.
Escort: a rooted gunner needs someone watching its sides while it sweeps.
On the enemy team, vehicles and lobbed-fire units become the counter-picks to a heavy gunner holding a choke.
controls: Q: start the burst; it fires on its own along your aim for its duration (or, rooted, sweep the arc with the mouse).
Rooted variant: hold Q and drag to set the arc's width before releasing; a wider arc keeps you locked longer.
Primary fire stays the ordinary gun; the key adds rate and suppression, not a new weapon.
feedback: From above, the swept area shows as a fan or lane of dense tracers with a faint tint on the ground for as long as it lasts.
Suppressed enemies show a marker over their head that fills as suppression builds and flashes when they are pinned (Iron Harvest added such a marker to portraits and overhead in Change Log #20).
The suppressed player's own screen shows the effect through weapon sway and a pinned icon, not by blurring the whole view.
A distinct heavy, rising gun sound when the burst starts, heard from well off screen.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS originals suppression slows whole squads that the AI moves; on a player it must limit speed and aim in ways the player can see and fight, not take control away, or it feels like being stunned for seconds.
Battlefield's history shows players hate heavy screen blur and aim loss; keep the penalty to sway, spread and slower movement, and make it fade quickly once the fire stops.
RTS suppression often ends in a pinned state that lasts until the fire stops; in a shooter, pinned should still allow crawling to cover, so the victim always has a move.
Iron Harvest's Grimbart sets the arc's width by order; for a player the arc is aimed and dragged live with the mouse.
Suppression is invisible in many RTS games except as an icon; from a top-down camera the swept area and the suppressed enemies must both be drawn clearly.

team_play.notes: Suppression is worth little alone: it holds enemies so teammates can flank, throw explosives or take ground, and the rooted gunner needs someone guarding its sides. The enemy team answers by picking armour and lobbed fire.

notes: Needs a suppression value per player that builds from fire passing near them (not only hits) and decays when the fire stops, decided on the server.
Area sweeps need cheap tests of which players a fan or lane of fire covers each tick, without simulating every bullet.
Clear rules for who is immune (vehicles, players in buildings or closed cabins) and how cover changes the build-up.
Bots must react to suppression (seek cover, stop pushing) or the pattern only works against humans.
Too strong a penalty makes a single gunner lock down a whole lane and turns fights into waiting games; Battlefield cut its effect back after complaints.
Several gunners stacking suppression on one choke can make it impassable for infantry.
Too weak and the key is only a damage burst; the pinning has to matter for teammates to play around it.
Players must tell suppression apart from damage and from a stun: an overhead marker and visible sway carry it.
The victim must see where the suppressing fire comes from, so they know which way cover is.

variants.name: Raking burst
variants.summary: The base form: on a key, for a few seconds your gun fires faster and pins much harder, but hits less often; you can still move slowly.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes Riflemen Suppression Fire

variants.name: Rooted sweep
variants.summary: Root yourself and sweep a frontal arc you set; the wider the arc, the longer you stay locked in place firing.

adds_weaknesses.why: Rooted for the whole sweep and facing one arc, so a flanker or lobbed fire from outside the arc catches it standing still.

variants.name: Single-target pin
variants.summary: Concentrate fire on one enemy, which is suppressed gradually or at once while the effect lasts.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes 2 Rear Echelon Volley Fire; Dawn of War II Shoota Boyz Aiming? Wotz Dat?

variants.name: Pin and punish
variants.summary: The pinned target loses aim, and if it moves while pinned you get a free reaction shot at it.

variants.name: Spotting suppression
variants.summary: Enemies you suppress are also marked for your whole team for as long as the suppression lasts.
variants.seen_in: Battlefield 1 Support Pin Down perk; Battlefield V machine gunners (both from the always-on weapon effect, not a key)

variants.name: Knockdown barrage
variants.summary: Rake an area with explosive rounds that knock soldiers off their feet instead of pinning them.
variants.seen_in: Dawn of War II Dreadnought Assault Cannon Barrage (explosive sweep with knockback; no suppression named)

adds_strengths.why: Pins enemy infantry in a lane or at one target for a few seconds, so teammates can flank or finish them.

adds_weaknesses.why: Rooted, inaccurate or busy while the burst lasts, and the key has a long wait, so the push comes right after it ends.

counters.why: Soldiers are what suppression slows and pins; Company of Heroes and Dawn of War II use it to hold infantry for a flank.

countered_by.why: Vehicles cannot be suppressed in Dawn of War II, so armour drives through the fire.
Attacks that need no aim, such as grenades, still land while pinned (XCOM), and the gunner stands still for them.
Reasoned: the shooter is rooted or busy in one direction, so a fast flanker from outside its arc reaches it unpinned.

open_questions: How hard should suppression hit a player's aim? In Battlefield, where ordinary gunfire suppresses, Battlefield 3 raised the penalty in a patch and cut it back after complaints, Battlefield 4 softened it, Battlefield 1 brought the penalties back, and Battlefield V dropped many of them. (Recommended: sway, spread and slower movement, no screen blur.)
Should pinned players still crawl, or be held fully until the fire stops as in the RTS sources? (Recommended: crawl toward cover.)
Should vehicles be fully immune, or should crews in open vehicles and emplacements be suppressible as in Foxhole?

Should suppressing an enemy also spot it for the team, or stay a pure control effect? In Battlefield 1 a Support perk spots the enemies its machine gun suppresses, and Battlefield V makes that spotting standard for machine gunners and vehicle gunners.

Foxhole and Battlefield make suppression an effect of ordinary gunfire, which is the suppress weapon trait rather than this key, so they are not listed as shooter analogues. Should Shamble Frontlines give suppression through the trait, this key, or both?

shooter_fit.reason: Suppression already lives in shooters as a weapon effect (Battlefield, Foxhole), and on a key it makes fire-and-manoeuvre teamwork readable; the risk is a penalty on aim that frustrates the target, so it must stay light and clearly shown.
